title: ASPIRe: the SFC's virtual-asset roadmap
md:
The Securities and Futures Commission's (SFC's) February 2025 plan of five pillars and 12 initiatives for Hong Kong's virtual-asset (VA) market.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | SFC [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Exploratory (roadmap); several initiatives since delivered through SFC circulars [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2, p.1] |
| Started | 19 Feb 2025 [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| Next official date | SFC custody surveillance system from H2 2026 (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| Covered in | A3, C1, C3, C6, C7, E1 |

## What it is

ASPIRe stands for five pillars: Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure and Relationships. Together they hold 12 initiatives. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] Access covers new licensing regimes for VA over-the-counter (OTC) dealing and custody, with custodian legislative preparation targeted for end-2025. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1] Safeguards includes exploring outcome-based custody standards in place of a fixed cold-storage ratio. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3] Products looks at professional-investor-only derivatives, margin financing, staking and lending. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar P, Initiatives 6-8] Infrastructure covers regulatory reporting and surveillance tools such as wallet tracing. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar I, Initiative 9] Most items are framed as things the SFC will explore or consider, not rules. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 19 Feb 2025 | ASPIRe roadmap published | Exploratory | [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| 7 Apr 2025 | Staking guidance for VATPs and funds, framed under Pillar P | In force | [S:36753b22e10a, para 2] |
| 27 Jun 2025 | VA dealing and custodian consultations (Pillar A) | Superseded | [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1] |
| 15 Aug 2025 | SFC custody circular to VATPs cites Pillar S, Initiative 3 | In force | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Importance of resilient custody controls and expected standards' section, p.1] |
| 3 Nov 2025 | Shared order book and product-expansion circulars (Pillars A and P) | In force | [S:f09e57feb89b, paras 1, 4, p.1] |
| 11 Feb 2026 | VA financing, perpetual contracts and affiliated market makers | In force | [S:089ec86e2407, paras 2-4, p.1] |
| H2 2026 | SFC digital-asset custody surveillance system | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| 2027 | CrypTech market and AML surveillance components | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- The roadmap itself binds no one. Bank duties come only from the circulars and conditions that implement it. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]
- VA financing now reaches banks too. Registered institutions (RIs) dealing in VAs may offer VA-backed margin financing to existing securities margin clients, under HKMA conditions. [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (2), (4) and fn 5]
- Staked client assets must sit in segregated accounts at an SFC-licensed platform or an Authorized Institution. [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4-5]
- VA trading platform (VATP) perpetual contracts are for professional investors only, and margin may be posted in HKMA-regulated tokenised deposits. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements']
- Pillar A's licensing initiatives are now the four VA intermediary regimes, in which banks would register rather than be licensed. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** ASPIRe is a roadmap; watch for the circulars that implement it, since those carry the obligations. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]
- **To business heads:** Delivered items so far include staking, shared order books, VA financing and professional-investor perpetuals. [S:36753b22e10a, para 2]; [S:089ec86e2407, paras 2-4, p.1]
- **To the CEO:** The SFC calls its structured, roadmap-based approach essential to growing the market. [S:089ec86e2407, para 2, p.1]
- **To Risk:** Outcome-based custody standards remain exploratory; today's VATP custody circular already applies. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]; [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7]

title: Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) and amended CRS
md:
Hong Kong's bill to bring in the OECD's yearly crypto-asset tax reporting standard and to update the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) that banks already follow.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and Inland Revenue Department (IRD) [S:252a7f86684e, paras 4, 7] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Bill before LegCo (First Reading 3 Jun 2026; no passage recorded) [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2] |
| Started | Commitment to the OECD Global Forum, 13 Dec 2024 [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4] |
| Next official date | 1 Jan 2027: CARF duties start, if the bill passes [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] |
| Covered in | D5, A3, E1, E3 |

## What it is

CARF is a standard of the OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) for yearly exchange of crypto-asset tax data between tax authorities. Hong Kong said it would legislate by 2026 and start exchanges from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4] The bill defines a Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider (RCASP) as a business that carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers. That includes acting as counterparty, broker or trading venue. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"] A Hong Kong RCASP would register, run due diligence, file returns and keep records. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50N-50O] Central bank digital currencies and specified e-money products are outside CARF but join the amended CRS. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 1.5, 4.3] If passed, CARF starts on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 Dec 2024 | Hong Kong commits to CARF; first exchanges from 2028 | Stated target | [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4] |
| 9 Dec 2025 | FSTB–IRD consultation (to 6 Feb 2026) | Superseded | [S:252a7f86684e, paras 4, 7] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget: amendment bill in the first half of 2026 | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108] |
| 22 May 2026 | Bill gazetted | Bill before LegCo | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| 3 Jun 2026 | First Reading; Second Reading debate adjourned | Bill before LegCo | [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2] |
| 1 Jan 2027 | Part 2 (CARF) commences, if passed | Bill before LegCo | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] |
| 1 Jan 2028 | Part 3 (amended CRS) commences, if passed | Bill before LegCo | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Map whether any group entity, as a business, carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers, including as an intermediary. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- Test each such entity, including branches, against the Hong Kong nexus rules. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
- A Hong Kong RCASP must register by 31 January of the year after it first meets a nexus test. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)]
- New customers need tax-residence self-certifications; existing users within 12 months of start. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- Under amended CRS, crypto-linked derivatives become financial assets and CBDCs and specified e-money join the depository-account concept. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5]
- Returns and registration go to the IRD, not the HKMA or SFC. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement']
- Using a service provider is not, on its own, a reasonable excuse for a failure. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The bill is not yet law. If passed, CARF duties start 1 January 2027 and amended CRS 1 January 2028. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]
- **To business heads:** Any customer crypto exchange service, even as intermediary, can make the entity an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- **To the CEO:** Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024, with first data exchanges targeted from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]
- **To Risk:** Fines can scale: $500 a day for continuing failures, or $1,000 per affected user for due-diligence breaches. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]

## Key documents

1. Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026 — LegCo / IRD — gazetted 22 May 2026 — read Clause 1, ss.50M-50R, 80R and 82E-82F — https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/pdf/carf/Inland%20Revenue%20(Amendment)%20(Crypto-Asset%20Reporting%20Framework%20and%20Amended%20Common%20Reporting%20Standard)%20Bill%202026(eng).pdf
2. Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework page — IRD — undated — read the Overview, due diligence, registration and penalty sections — https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/tax/dta_carf.htm
3. Implementation of CARF and Amendments in Relation to CRS (consultation paper) — FSTB and IRD — 9 Dec 2025 — read paras 4.3-4.18 and Chapter 6 — https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/government/publication/consultation/docs/2026/crypto-framework.pdf
4. Hong Kong commits to implementing Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework — FSTB — 13 Dec 2024 — read paras 1-4 — https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202412/13/P2024121300491.htm

title: CBDC research and cross-border digital money pilots
md:
The HKMA's research projects on central bank digital currency (CBDC) and tokenised money (Aurum, Sela, Genesis, Inthanon-LionRock), plus the cross-boundary e-CNY pilot and the 2026 Shanghai cooperation.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) with the BIS Innovation Hub (BISIH), other central banks and Mainland bodies [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']; [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Research (Aurum, Sela, Genesis); Pilot (e-CNY); Exploratory (Shanghai MoU) [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']; [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1]; [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| Started | Q4 2019 (Inthanon-LionRock) [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1] |
| Next official date | None stated; e-CNY wallet-limit talks have no confirmed date [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5)] |
| Covered in | E2, C5, E3 |

## What it is

Project Aurum, with the BISIH and a local research institute, built a two-tier prototype. It paired a bank-to-bank layer with retail e-wallets, and its report came out in October 2022. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] Project Sela, with the Bank of Israel, tested letting non-bank "Access Enablers" connect directly to a central bank ledger. [S:8146b4a87d45, press release para 2] Sela's report says it reflects no HKMA policy decision on e-HKD. [S:8146b4a87d45, report Section 1, footnote 5] Project Genesis was a 2021 bond tokenisation proof of concept with the BISIH, and the 2023 Government tokenised bond built on it. [S:a0841967c871, quote from Eddie Yue, p.1] Inthanon-LionRock, with the Bank of Thailand, tested CBDC cross-border payments and grew into mBridge. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1] The cross-boundary e-CNY pilot lets Hong Kong residents open personal Mainland digital renminbi wallets and top them up through the Faster Payment System (FPS). [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1; Annex 1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2019 | Inthanon-LionRock begins with the Bank of Thailand | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1] |
| 2021 | Project Genesis proof of concept completed | Research | [S:a0841967c871, quote from Eddie Yue, p.1] |
| Oct 2022 | Project Aurum report | Research | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] |
| 12 Sep 2023 | Project Sela report | Research | [S:8146b4a87d45, press release paras 1-2] |
| 20 Oct 2023 | HKMA sets up CBDC Expert Group with local universities | Research | [S:28af6d5e86cb, para 1] |
| 17 May 2024 | Cross-boundary e-CNY pilot expanded | Pilot | [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1] |
| 8 Oct 2025 | Government: e-CNY limit relaxation still under discussion | Pilot | [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5)] |
| 2 Mar 2026 | HKMA–Shanghai Data Bureau–blockchain centre MoU on digitised cargo trade and finance | Exploratory | [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| 25 Mar 2026 | Government reports about 80,000 e-CNY wallets and 18 top-up banks | Pilot | [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Research projects create no obligations; their designs are not policy decisions. [S:8146b4a87d45, report Section 1, footnote 5]
- If the bank is an FPS top-up bank, note that tier-4 e-CNY wallets cap balances at RMB10,000 and allow no person-to-person transfers. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2]
- Per-transaction and yearly e-CNY limits are RMB2,000 and RMB50,000; any relaxation has no confirmed date. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5)]
- The Shanghai MoU will look at a cross-border platform and electronic bills of lading under Project Ensemble, linked to trade data. Trade-finance teams may be asked to take part. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]
- The Government expects stablecoins, e-CNY and tokenised deposits to develop different roles, driven by market forces. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (3)]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Sela and Aurum are research, not rules; Sela says so expressly. [S:8146b4a87d45, report Section 1, footnote 5]
- **To business heads:** About 80,000 e-CNY wallets were registered with Hong Kong numbers by end-January 2026, with 18 banks supporting FPS top-ups. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]
- **To the CEO:** The Shanghai MoU links Ensemble to Mainland trade-finance data work. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]
- **To Risk:** e-CNY wallets block person-to-person transfers and cap balances, which limits misuse paths to monitor. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2]

## Key documents

1. HKMA Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) page — HKMA — updated Sep 2026 — read 'Collaborative Projects' and the Inthanon-LionRock section — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/key-functions/international-financial-centre/fintech/central-bank-digital-currency/
2. Project Sela: an accessible and secure retail CBDC ecosystem — HKMA, Bank of Israel and BISIH — 12 Sep 2023 — read Section 1 and its footnotes — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2023/20230912e3a1.pdf
3. Expanding the cross-boundary e-CNY pilot in Hong Kong — HKMA — 17 May 2024 — read para 1 and Annexes 1-2 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/05/20240517-3/
4. HKMA, Shanghai Data Bureau and National Technology Innovation Center for Blockchain MoU — HKMA — 2 Mar 2026 — read paras 1-2 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/03/20260302-3/

title: CMU OmniClear digital asset platform and tokenised Exchange Fund Bills
md:
Plans to add a digital-asset platform to Hong Kong's bond settlement system, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), and to test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | CMU OmniClear Limited, which runs the CMU for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA); HKMA for the Exchange Fund Bills tests [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-3]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Stated target [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| Started | CMU OmniClear set up 18 Oct 2024 [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-2] |
| Next official date | Platform "this year" (2026); Exchange Fund Bills tests by end-2026 (both stated targets) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| Covered in | C5, A3, E1, E3 |

## What it is

CMU OmniClear is owned through the Exchange Fund and runs the CMU under contract to the HKMA. [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-2] The HKMA keeps ownership of the CMU system, its legal ties with members and its policy decisions. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 4, p.1] Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) is taking a 20% stake in the holding company; the Exchange Fund keeps 80%. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2, p.1] The 2026-27 Budget said CMU OmniClear would set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for digital bond issuance and settlement. It would later cover other digital assets and link to regional tokenisation platforms. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] The 2026 Policy Address repeats the platform target. It also says the HKMA will test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end, covering more than $1.3 trillion of bills, so banks can use them round the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] The CMU already runs a DLT platform: the HKMC's June 2026 digital bonds were created and settled on it. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 4]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Feb 2023 | First tokenised Government bond clears through the CMU with statutory finality | Issued | [S:a0841967c871, para 4] |
| 18 Oct 2024 | HKMA establishes CMU OmniClear Limited | In force | [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-2] |
| 4 Mar 2025 | CMU OmniClear–HKEX MoU on post-trade infrastructure | Exploratory | [S:74db8f7570bd, paras 2-3] |
| 12 Nov 2025 | HKEX to take 20% of CMU OmniClear Holdings | Issued (announcement) | [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2, p.1] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget: digital asset platform to be set up in 2026 | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] |
| 10 Jun 2026 | HKMC digital bonds created on a CMU-operated DLT platform | Issued | [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 4] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: platform this year; tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests by year-end | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Nothing binding yet. Both items are stated targets, and the corpus holds no platform rulebook or test design. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]
- The Exchange Fund Bills tests are aimed at banks' round-the-clock asset and liability management, so treasury and liquidity teams are the likely users. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- A bond issued on a CMU-operated DLT platform meets one of the basic conditions of the Digital Bond Grant Scheme. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3]
- CMU settlement carries statutory settlement finality. A DLT platform gets that only if the HKMA designates it; otherwise finality must be agreed by contract. [S:b7e1bb6b44ae, report paras 37-38]
- For customer-facing tokenised bond products, the HKMA tokenised-products circular and prior HKMA discussion still apply. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Implementation', p.6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** No new rules yet; watch for CMU platform terms and any HKMA note on the Exchange Fund Bills tests. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]
- **To business heads:** The platform is meant as a one-stop service for digital bond issuance and settlement. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA plans to test tokenising more than $1.3 trillion of Exchange Fund Bills by end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- **To Risk:** Check whether any DLT settlement venue has designated status before relying on statutory finality. [S:b7e1bb6b44ae, report paras 37-38]

## Key documents

1. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — HKSAR Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read para 35 (pp.22-23) — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf
2. 2026-27 Budget — Financial Secretary — 25 Feb 2026 — read paras 112-114 — https://www.budget.gov.hk/2026/eng/pdf/e_budget_speech_2026-27.pdf
3. HKMA Establishes CMU OmniClear Limited — HKMA — 18 Oct 2024 — read paras 1-3 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/10/20241018-5/
4. HKMA introduces HKEX as a strategic shareholder in CMU OmniClear Holdings Limited — HKMA — 12 Nov 2025 — read paras 2-4 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251112-3/

title: Digital Bond Grant Scheme (DBGS)
md:
An HKMA subsidy that refunds part of the cost of issuing a digital bond in Hong Kong.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (initial three-year period) [S:5a0563de8142, p.1 fn 1] |
| Started | Applications opened 28 Nov 2024; covers bonds issued on or after 16 Oct 2024 [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 1, footnote 1] |
| Next official date | End of the initial three years from 28 Nov 2024 (no renewal decision in the corpus) [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 3] |
| Covered in | C5, E3 |

## What it is

The DBGS refunds half of eligible issuance costs for a digital bond. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] The cap is HK$1.25 million for a Half Grant, where only the basic conditions are met. It rises to HK$2.5 million for a Full Grant, where the additional conditions are also met. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] Each issuer group can claim for no more than two issues. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] To qualify at all, at least half of the lead arrangers must be recognised Hong Kong arrangers. The bond also needs a DLT team with real Hong Kong presence, or must use a CMU-run DLT platform. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3] The HKMA keeps full discretion over eligibility and grant amounts, and may change the scheme. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Oct 2024 | Scheme announced in the Policy Address; bonds issued from this date are covered | In force | [S:5a0563de8142, p.1 fn 1] |
| 28 Nov 2024 | HKMA launches the DBGS and opens applications | In force | [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 1, footnote 1] |
| 28 Nov 2024 | Guideline on the DBGS issued | In force | [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget says the HKMA will use the DBGS to encourage more digital bond issues | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97] |
| 16 Jul 2026 | HKMA one-page scheme summary published | In force | [S:2397140df663, p.1] |
| Nov 2027 | Initial three-year period ends (three years from 28 Nov 2024) | Stated target | [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 3] |

## What it means for your bank

- If the bank arranges bonds, arranger roles matter: half or more of lead arrangers must be recognised in Hong Kong for the issue to qualify. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3]
- The Full Grant needs a DLT platform provider outside the issuer's group of associates. A bank issuing on its own group platform would not meet that test. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
- The Full Grant also needs at least HK$1 billion in size, five or more unrelated investors, and a listing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) or an SFC-licensed VA trading platform. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
- Fees paid to associates are not eligible expenses. [S:633ce27d4f9b, Guideline s.4, p.5]
- A green digital bond can claim general issuance costs under the DBGS or Track I of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, not both. [S:5a0563de8142, s.4, p.5]
- The formal application must be filed within three months of issue. An optional pre-application consultation with the HKMA is available. [S:5a0563de8142, s.5, p.6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The grant is a subsidy, not a licence or approval. The HKMA keeps absolute discretion on eligibility and amount. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1]
- **To business heads:** Clients can recover up to HK$2.5 million per issue, for at most two issues per issuer group. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2]
- **To the CEO:** The Government links the scheme to its aim of more digital bond issues in Hong Kong. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97]
- **To Risk:** Using an associated DLT platform caps the grant at the Half Grant level. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]

## Key documents

title: Digital bonds: Genesis, Evergreen and the public-sector issues
md:
Hong Kong's run of bond tokenisation work, from the 2021 Project Genesis test to three Government green bond deals and the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation's (HKMC's) 2026 digital bond.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for the HKSAR Government; HKMC for its own issue [S:a0841967c871, para 8]; [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Issued (latest issue settled 15 Jun 2026); Government says issuance will be regularised [S:6aa27ee8b400, Annex]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(i)] |
| Started | 2021 (Project Genesis proof of concept) [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] |
| Next official date | No date given; the Budget says tokenised bonds will keep being issued on a regular basis [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97] |
| Covered in | C5, E2, A3, E3 |

## What it is

The HKMA began bond tokenisation in 2021 with a proof of concept alongside the BIS Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] Project Evergreen then produced a HK$800 million tokenised green bond in February 2023, described as the first tokenised bond from any government. [S:a0841967c871, para 1] It settled on a T+1 basis through the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), which carries statutory settlement finality. [S:a0841967c871, paras 3-4] The HKMA's August 2023 report found that existing Hong Kong law prescribes no paper form for debt securities. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 28, pp.11-12] A multi-currency issue of about HK$6 billion followed in February 2024. [S:4290ec1111e3, key features] In November 2025 a HK$10 billion issue became the first digital bond to offer settlement in e-HKD and e-CNY. [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 4-5] In June 2026 the HKMC priced about HK$12 billion of digital bonds created on a CMU-run platform. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 1, 4]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | Project Genesis proof of concept with BIS Innovation Hub | Research | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] |
| 31 Oct 2022 | Policy Statement names a tokenised green bond pilot | Superseded | [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 10-11] |
| 16 Feb 2023 | HK$800m tokenised Government green bond settles | Issued | [S:a0841967c871, para 1; terms table, p.2] |
| 24 Aug 2023 | Evergreen report on bond tokenisation | Research | [S:a0b44be27c40, para 26] |
| 7 Feb 2024 | About HK$6bn multi-currency digital green bonds priced | Issued | [S:4290ec1111e3, para 12] |
| 28 Nov 2024 | EvergreenHub knowledge repository launched | In force | [S:64cf94cf2036, para 5] |
| 10 Nov 2025 | HK$10bn digital green bonds priced, with e-HKD/e-CNY settlement option | Issued | [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 1-5] |
| 10 Jun 2026 | HKMC prices about HK$12bn digital bonds (issued 15 Jun 2026) | Issued | [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1; Annex] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: digital bond issuance to be regularised | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(i)] |

## What it means for your bank

- In Evergreen, only custodians that were CMU participants and onboarded to the platform could open token accounts. Other investors held through the custodian's own books. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 45, p.16]
- Where investors join the platform directly, the operator and any custodian are expected to run know-your-customer (KYC) checks and support AML/CFT compliance. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 44, p.16]
- Statutory finality comes only from a designated clearing and settlement system; otherwise finality rests on contract. [S:b7e1bb6b44ae, report paras 37-38]
- Existing securities licensing and offering rules apply to digital bond distribution as they do to ordinary bonds. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 23-24, p.11]
- Selling tokenised bonds to customers falls under the HKMA tokenised-products circular, including prior discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Implementation', p.6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Digital bonds carry no new licence category; ordinary securities rules apply. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 23-24, p.11]
- **To business heads:** Sixteen financial institutions arranged the HKMC deal. Investors could use existing CMU links to Euroclear and Clearstream, and settlement fell from T+5 to T+3. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 5, 8]
- **To the CEO:** The Policy Address says Hong Kong-issued digital bonds took almost half the global market from 2025 to mid-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35]
- **To Risk:** Evergreen flags untested DLT platform risk and asks for continuity plans covering disruption and platform migration. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 46-47, p.17]

## Key documents

1. Bond Tokenisation in Hong Kong (Project Evergreen report) — HKMA — 24 Aug 2023 — read paras 23-47 on law, custody and settlement — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2023/20230824e3a1.pdf
2. HKSAR Government's Third Digital Green Bonds Offering — HKMA — 11 Nov 2025 — read paras 1-7 and key features — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251111-6/

title: e-HKD (digital Hong Kong dollar)
md:
The HKMA's long-running work on a possible Hong Kong central bank digital currency (CBDC), now focused on wholesale use by financial institutions.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Exploratory (retail); wholesale is the stated priority [S:6bd9e65817c4, paras 4-5]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] |
| Started | 2017 (Project LionRock) [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project LionRock' section] |
| Next official date | Real-value e-HKD payments for after-hours derivatives with HKEX targeted in 2026 (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] |
| Covered in | E2, A3, E1, E3 |

## What it is

The HKMA began in 2017 with a wholesale proof of concept, Project LionRock. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project LionRock' section] It then consulted on a retail e-HKD through a 2021 technical paper and a 2022 policy paper. The technical paper proposed a two-tier model in which banks distribute e-HKD. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4] In September 2022 the HKMA set a three-rail approach. It found existing law not certain enough for issuing digital legal tender. [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section] Industry pilots ran in two phases, and the project was renamed e-HKD+ in September 2024 to cover tokenised deposits too. [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] In October 2025 the HKMA said the near-term priority is wholesale payments, not retail. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] It has not decided whether or when to launch a retail e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | Project LionRock wholesale proof of concept | Research | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project LionRock' section] |
| 4 Oct 2021 | Technical paper proposes two-tier design | Superseded | [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-5] |
| 27 Apr 2022 | Policy and design paper | Research | [S:3b42966a786e, Section 7] |
| 20 Sep 2022 | Three-rail approach set | Research | [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section] |
| 18 May 2023 | Phase 1 pilots start with 16 firms | Research | [S:933b9f10e3b2, para 1] |
| 30 Oct 2023 | Phase 1 report | Research | [S:9f8886b0fb21, Executive Summary, p.6] |
| 23 Sep 2024 | Phase 2 starts; project renamed e-HKD+ | Research | [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] |
| 28 Oct 2025 | Phase 2 report; wholesale uses prioritised | Research | [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] |
| 11 Nov 2025 | Government digital bond offers e-HKD settlement option | Issued | [S:ac6cd085a325, para 4] |
| H1 2026 | Groundwork for possible retail use to be finished | Stated target | [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 5] |
| 2026 | Real-value e-HKD payments for after-hours derivatives with HKEX | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] |

## What it means for your bank

- There is no binding e-HKD rule. The designs are research papers and pilot findings. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']
- The April 2022 paper ruled out full anonymity so that e-HKD could support AML/CFT compliance, and floated tiered wallets. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.3]
- In any retail distribution role, the designs place customer due diligence and record-keeping on the intermediary. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4]
- Phase 2 found the public sees e-HKD and tokenised deposits in a similar light, because of high trust in banks. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 3]
- The HKMA says it will publish common token standards from the e-HKD Industry Forum. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** No retail e-HKD decision exists; designs expect distributing banks to run customer due diligence. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']; [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4]
- **To business heads:** The HKMA's e-HKD focus is now wholesale: tokenisation and cross-border settlement. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
- **To the CEO:** The Government's November 2025 digital bond was the first to settle using e-HKD and e-CNY. [S:ac6cd085a325, para 4]
- **To Risk:** Phase 2 found privacy tools raised gas fees by up to 320 times. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', p.31]

title: Project Ensemble
md:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA's) programme to let banks settle tokenised deposits and tokenised assets with each other, now running live-money trades as EnsembleTX.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA, with an industry Architecture Community [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 2-3] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot (EnsembleTX runs throughout 2026) [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |
| Started | 7 Mar 2024 [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] |
| Next official date | Around end-2026: 24/7 operation and settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC) (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| Covered in | C5, E1, E2, A3, E3 |

## What it is

Ensemble looks at new market infrastructure so that banks can settle tokenised money with each other using wholesale central bank money. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] Its first focus is tokenised deposits, meaning digital versions of ordinary commercial bank deposits. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] The HKMA set up an Architecture Community in May 2024 to agree shared industry standards. [S:0169bc8fbb4d, para 2] A Sandbox followed in August 2024. Community banks linked their tokenised-deposit platforms to it and tested two settlement modes: PvP (payment versus payment) and DvP (delivery versus payment). [S:460620ab7f2b, para 2] In November 2025 the project moved to EnsembleTX, a pilot using real value. It starts with tokenised money market fund trades and treasury and liquidity uses. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-2] At first, banks settle with each other through Hong Kong's HKD RTGS (real-time gross settlement) system. The HKMA plans a gradual move to round-the-clock settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 Mar 2024 | HKMA unveils Project Ensemble | Superseded (by EnsembleTX) | [S:5a9cad53f2be, paras 2-3] |
| 7 May 2024 | Ensemble Architecture Community formed | Superseded | [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 2-3] |
| 27 Jun 2024 | MoU with Banque de France (BDF) on linking its DL3S system with the Ensemble Sandbox | Exploratory | [S:0ed273d6f63f, paras 2-3] |
| 28 Aug 2024 | Ensemble Sandbox launched, with four test themes | Superseded | [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 2-3] |
| 28 Oct 2024 | Tie-ups with Banco Central do Brasil (BCB, Drex) and Bank of Thailand (BoT, Project San) | Exploratory | [S:8d9f12b43ada, para 1]; [S:aabff1db2350, para 3] |
| 13 Nov 2025 | EnsembleTX real-value pilot launched | Pilot | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget says the HKMA will keep upgrading EnsembleTX towards 24/7 settlement | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 109] |
| 2 Mar 2026 | HKMA–Shanghai MoU, including e-bills of lading under Ensemble | Exploratory | [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| Around end-2026 | CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation under EnsembleTX | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| By end-2026 | Tokenised-deposit trade-finance pilot with the Mainland | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 99] |

## What it means for your bank

- Participation is by invitation and commitment. The seven named Tokenised Deposit Banks each agree to offer tokenised deposits to Hong Kong customers and settle interbank deals in EnsembleTX with real value. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A] The HKMA invites firms with new real-value use cases to join. [S:8b67e8dc510f, CE quote]
- Offering tokenised deposits to customers brings in the HKMA's tokenised-products circular, which expects due diligence, disclosure and early discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1; 'Implementation', p.6]
- For the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR), tokenised deposits that are a legal claim on the bank can be reported like other deposits, but never get the stable-deposit outflow rate. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]
- The HKMA expects DLT risk controls on network choice, smart contracts, settlement finality and key security. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 2-8]
- Before launch, the Supervisory Incubator lets a bank check its tokenised-deposit risk controls with a dedicated HKMA team. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** EnsembleTX is a pilot, not a rulebook. Customer-facing tokenised deposits still fall under the HKMA tokenised-products circular and need prior HKMA discussion. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1; p.6]
- **To business heads:** The pilot starts with tokenised money market funds and real-time treasury uses, and the HKMA is inviting new real-value use cases. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 2 and CE quote]
- **To the CEO:** The Policy Address targets CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation in EnsembleTX by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- **To Risk:** Tokenised deposits never get stable-deposit LCR treatment; outflows are reported separately if holders cannot always be identified. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]

1. HKMA announces the new phase of Project Ensemble (EnsembleTX) — HKMA — 13 Nov 2025 — read the full release for scope and settlement design — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251113-3/
2. Annex A and Annex B to the EnsembleTX release — HKMA — 13 Nov 2025 — read both annexes for the participant lists and bank commitments — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251113e3a1.pdf
3. HKMA unveils Project Ensemble — HKMA — 7 Mar 2024 — read paras 2-6 for the original aims — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/03/20240307-5/
4. HKMA launches Project Ensemble Sandbox — HKMA — 28 Aug 2024 — read paras 2-4 and the Annex for test themes — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/08/20240828-3/
5. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — HKSAR Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read paras 50 and 99 — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

title: Project mBridge
md:
A shared platform on which several central banks' digital currencies can settle cross-border payments and foreign exchange (FX) trades between banks.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA with the Bank of Thailand (BoT), the People's Bank of China Digital Currency Institute (PBoC DCI), the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) and, as of the 2024 MVP, the BIS Innovation Hub (BISIH); the Saudi Central Bank joined in 2024 [S:db56d97e2206, fn 1, paras 3-4] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot; the Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |
| Started | Q4 2019 as Inthanon-LionRock; renamed in Feb 2021 [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1] |
| Next official date | None stated; no timetable for wider participation [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5)] |
| Covered in | E2, E3 |

## What it is

The project began as Inthanon-LionRock, run by the HKMA and the BoT. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1] In February 2021 the PBoC DCI and the CBUAE joined, and it became the m-CBDC Bridge. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1] The platform tests real-time, round-the-clock FX payment-versus-payment deals across several jurisdictions. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project mBridge' section] In the 2022 pilot, 20 banks in four jurisdictions made more than 160 payment and FX trades worth over US$22 million. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive Summary, p.4] The platform reached minimum viable product (MVP) stage in June 2024, with a validating node in each founding jurisdiction. [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1, 3] In October 2025 the Government told LegCo that participating banks set their own fees. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2019 | Inthanon-LionRock begins (HKMA + BoT) | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1] |
| Jan 2020 | Inthanon-LionRock report | Superseded | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section] |
| 23 Feb 2021 | PBoC DCI and CBUAE join; renamed m-CBDC Bridge | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, para 1] |
| 28 Sep 2021 | Interim report on faster, cheaper payments | Research | [S:0cfb7eee08a3, paras 2-3] |
| 15 Aug 2022 | Six-week real-value pilot begins | Pilot | [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16] |
| 26 Oct 2022 | Pilot results published | Pilot | [S:2c7f151156dc, para 2] |
| 30 Oct 2023 | mBridge update brochure | Pilot | [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.10] |
| 5 Jun 2024 | MVP reached; Saudi Central Bank joins | Pilot | [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1, 4] |
| 8 Oct 2025 | Government: mBridge is part of Hong Kong's market infrastructure | Pilot | [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Each bank runs its own sanctions, anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) checks before sending or confirming a payment. The platform does not. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- The platform only records a pass or fail certificate from the bank's off-platform check. Each jurisdiction's AML, CTF and sanctions laws still apply. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35]
- Know-your-customer (KYC), AML and CFT work stays in the bank's own systems, off the bridge. [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]
- Only a domestically licensed bank can ask for issue or redemption of its home jurisdiction's CBDC. Check each counterparty's role. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, pp.31-32]
- Private firms can propose add-on technology or use cases through a BISIH form. [S:db56d97e2206, para 5]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** mBridge leaves AML and sanctions screening to each bank, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- **To business heads:** Participating banks set their own mBridge service fees. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- **To the CEO:** mBridge reached MVP in June 2024; the Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1]; [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- **To Risk:** The 2022 pilot ran on one cloud environment in Hong Kong, flagged as a privacy and governance issue to revisit. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.3, p.33]

1. Project mBridge: Connecting economies through CBDC — HKMA and partners — Oct 2022 — read ss.6.4, 6.5.2, 7.1 and 7.2 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2022/20221026e3a1.pdf
2. Project mBridge reaches MVP stage — HKMA — 5 Jun 2024 — read paras 1-5 and footnote 1 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/06/20240605-4/
3. Project mBridge Update: Experimenting with a multi-CBDC platform for cross-border payments — BISIH and partners — Oct 2023 — read pp.2-3 on roles and compliance — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/financial-infrastructure/mBridge_publication.pdf
4. LCQ21: e-CNY wallets — HKSAR Government — 8 Oct 2025 — read Reply (4) — https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202510/08/P2025100800250.htm

title: Government policy statements and Policy Address items
md:
The Government's own strategy papers on digital assets: the 2022 Policy Statement, Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) in 2025, and the digital-asset targets in the 2025 and 2026 Policy Addresses.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB); Chief Executive for Policy Addresses [S:f587b828e3fa, para 4]; [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49-50] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Stated target (Policy Statement 2.0 and 2026 Policy Address); 2022 statement superseded [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6]; [S:f587b828e3fa, para 4] |
| Started | 31 Oct 2022 [S:f587b828e3fa, para 4] |
| Next official date | VA dealing, custody, advisory and management bill "later this year" (2026) [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| Covered in | A3, A1, E1, E3 |

## What it is

The 2022 Policy Statement set the principle of treating the same activity and risks under the same regulation. It also promised mandatory licensing for VA service providers. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6] It named three pilots: NFT issuance, a tokenised Government green bond and e-HKD. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 10-11] Policy Statement 2.0 (June 2025) set out the LEAP framework. LEAP means legal and regulatory streamlining, expanding tokenised products, advancing use cases, and people and partnership development. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 4] It named the SFC as lead licensing authority for digital-asset dealing and custody, with the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] It also switched the Government's term to *digital assets*. The legal term in the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO) stays *virtual asset*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1] The 2026 Policy Address adds dated targets for the HKMA and SFC. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35, 49-51]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31 Oct 2022 | Policy Statement on Development of VA in Hong Kong | Superseded | [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6] |
| 26 Jun 2025 | Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) | Stated target | [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] |
| 17 Sep 2025 | 2025 Policy Address: bill for dealing and custodian licensing in 2026 | Stated target | [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex item 22] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | 2026-27 Budget restates 2026 bill target and CARF bill | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | 2026 Policy Address: tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests; CMU OmniClear platform | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | 2026 Policy Address: SFC to widen VA licensing, tokenised gold, stablecoin trading | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(i)-(iii)] |
| Around end-2026 | EnsembleTX CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| By 2029 | Customs DATAS and AMLAS analytics systems | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, Part II item 209] |

## What it means for your bank

- Policy statements and Policy Addresses create no obligations; they are delivered later through laws, guidelines and circulars. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49-51]
- Under PS 2.0 banks will register with the SFC for dealing and custody, with the HKMA as frontline regulator. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- The 2025 Policy Address said the HKMA would encourage banks to issue tokenised deposits and settle tokenised money market fund trades with them. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, para 103, p.40]
- The same paragraph said the HKMA would push banks to use the supervisory sandbox to improve their risk controls. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, para 103, p.40]
- The HKMA has separately asked each bank's board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Government now says *digital assets*, but AMLO still defines *virtual asset*; use the legal term in policies. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]
- **To business heads:** The SFC plans to let licensed platforms trade regulated stablecoins and use them to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- **To the CEO:** The Government's stated 2026 target is one bill for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management licensing. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- **To Risk:** Customs plans digital-asset transaction analytics by 2029, feeding a wider financial-crime data platform. [S:ef3648ff1610, Part II item 209]

title: Relevant Stablecoins: dealing, advice and trading
md:
The May 2026 HKMA and SFC package that eases how virtual-asset conduct rules apply to stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers, plus the stated plan for trading on licensed platforms.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for banks; Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for trading platforms and licensed corporations [S:a0bd48559762, opening paragraph, p.1]; [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (since 27 May 2026) [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| Started | 27 May 2026 [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] |
| Next official date | None fixed. Policy Address says the SFC will promote stablecoin trading on licensed platforms (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] |
| Covered in | C1, C4, B2, C7, E1 |

## What it is

A Relevant Stablecoin is a specified stablecoin whose issue is authorised under a Stablecoins Ordinance licence. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] After the Ordinance started, the two regulators reviewed how the joint virtual-asset (VA) circulars should apply to these coins, given their currency-pegged profile. [S:a0bd48559762, Background, pp.1-2] The HKMA's circular to registered institutions (RIs) updates the conduct terms into Appendices A1 and A2. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance', p.2] A separate HKMA letter points all Authorized Institutions (AIs) to the same standards. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] The SFC's circular 26EC26 covers VA trading platforms (VATPs) and licensed corporations (LCs), not banks. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] The HKMA letter says its guidance should not be read as treating these coins as investment products. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Aug 2025 | Stablecoins Ordinance commences | In force | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| 10 Apr 2026 | First two issuer licences take effect | In force | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] |
| 27 May 2026 | HKMA RI circular with Appendices A1/A2 | In force | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| 27 May 2026 | HKMA letter to all AIs | In force | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| 27 May 2026 | SFC circular 26EC26 to VATPs and LCs | In force | [S:19d52ade6849, paras 2, 12] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: SFC to promote stablecoin trading on licensed platforms and use in settling tokenised money market funds | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- An RI may now deal in a Relevant Stablecoin through the licensed issuer as well as through a VATP. [S:a0bd48559762, para (1), p.3]
- Relevant-Stablecoin-only dealing needs no Type 1 registration, but the Appendix A1 conduct terms still apply. [S:a0bd48559762, para (2), p.3]
- For accounts clearly ring-fenced as Relevant-Stablecoin-only, no VA knowledge test is needed. Adding any other VA brings back the full rules. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4]
- The bank must disclose each coin's stabilisation mechanism and redemption arrangements when dealing. [S:a0bd48559762, para (5), p.5]
- Advice must rest on the client's use case; commission rebates must not drive it. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]
- RIs must notify the HKMA and SFC before starting or materially changing these activities. Other AIs should discuss them with the HKMA first. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, 'Implementation', p.2]
- The relief does not cover other stablecoins, AIs that are not RIs, or an issuer dealing in its own coin. [S:a0bd48559762, footnote 3, p.2]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** We follow the HKMA RI circular, not 26EC26, which binds VATPs and LCs. Advance notice to both regulators is still required. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.9]
- **To business heads:** Ring-fenced stablecoin-only accounts need no knowledge test and no exposure limit. Mixing in other VAs removes that relief. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)-(b), pp.4-5]
- **To the CEO:** The Policy Address says the SFC will promote licensed-platform trading of regulated stablecoins, including for tokenised money market fund settlement. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- **To Risk:** Only coins from HKMA-licensed issuers qualify; check the register before dealing. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 5]

## Key documents

1. Virtual asset-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins (RI circular) — HKMA — 27 May 2026 — read all nine pages, especially paras (1)-(9) and Implementation — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf
2. Relevant Stablecoin-related Activities (letter to AIs) — HKMA — 27 May 2026 — read both pages — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-4-EN/20260527-4-EN.pdf
3. Circular on provision of Relevant Stablecoin service by VATPs and LCs (26EC26) — SFC — 27 May 2026 — read paras 2-12 for counterparty rules — https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC26
4. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — HKSAR Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read para 49 — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

title: Stablecoin issuer regime (Stablecoins Ordinance, Cap. 656)
md:
Hong Kong's licensing law for issuers of fiat-referenced stablecoins, from the 2024 sandbox through the Ordinance, the first licences, the public register, the review tribunal and complaint handling.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as licensing authority; Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) for policy and the Stablecoin Review Tribunal [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]; [S:16699fe49364, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (since 1 Aug 2025) [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Started | Discussion paper, 12 Jan 2022 [S:2b888e600616, Section 6] |
| Next official date | None fixed. Launch of licensed coins was expected mid-to-late 2026 [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, para 2] |
| Covered in | C4, B2, C3, D3, E3 |

## What it is

The Ordinance requires an HKMA licence to issue a fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) in Hong Kong. The same applies to an FRS referenced to the Hong Kong dollar, wherever it is issued. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2] Licensed issuers must back coins in full with segregated reserves, and must meet the reserve value of coins in circulation at all times. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1] Valid redemptions are met at par, generally within one business day. [S:240be6833157, para 3.3.3] Only listed permitted offerors may offer coins, and an Authorized Institution (AI) is one of them. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1] The HKMA licensed the first two issuers with effect from 10 April 2026. It says further licences will stay very limited. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1]; [S:193316443831, final paragraphs]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 Jan 2022 | HKMA discussion paper on crypto-assets and stablecoins | Superseded | [S:2b888e600616, Section 6] |
| 27 Dec 2023 | FSTB–HKMA consultation on issuer regime (to 29 Feb 2024) | Superseded | [S:167649d1bc28, para 3] |
| 12 Mar 2024 | Stablecoin issuer sandbox launched | Superseded | [S:f2a668eb3b93, Annex] |
| 17 Jul 2024 | Consultation conclusions published | Superseded | [S:54aa01e7396e, para 12.1] |
| 18 Jul 2024 | First three sandbox participant groups announced | Superseded | [S:cf1df12c1b58, paras 1-2] |
| 6 Dec 2024 | Stablecoins Bill gazetted | Superseded | [S:a9a82f2b38ce, para 1] |
| 21 May 2025 | LegCo passes the Bill | Superseded | [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 1] |
| 1 Aug 2025 | Ordinance and HKMA guidelines take effect | In force | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]; [S:6c3f349e4f90, para 1] |
| 1 Nov 2025 | Stablecoin Review Tribunal term begins (to 31 Oct 2028) | In force | [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3] |
| 10 Apr 2026 | First two issuer licences take effect; register published | In force | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] |
| Mid-to-late 2026 | Launch of licensed coins expected | Stated target | [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, para 2] |

## What it means for your bank

- As a permitted offeror, the bank may offer licensed-issuer coins to anyone. Other specified stablecoins go to professional investors only. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), paras 2-3]
- An AI can apply to issue. Overseas-incorporated AIs need no local subsidiary, and some criteria, such as financial resources, do not apply to AI applicants. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 6, 8]
- Before dealing, check that the issuer is on the HKMA register. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 5]
- Sandbox admission was never a licence or an endorsement. [S:f2a668eb3b93, Annex, Objectives, p.1]
- For its own holdings, the bank must notify the HKMA before first acquiring a new stablecoin type. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- The HKMA reviews escalated complaints about issuers but does not order compensation. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, 'Lodging Complaint with the HKMA' section]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Retail may only get coins from licensed issuers; we are a permitted offeror. Check the register before any deal. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 2]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 5]
- **To business heads:** Two issuers hold licences effective 10 April 2026. The HKMA says the total will remain very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:193316443831, final paragraphs]
- **To the CEO:** An AI may apply to issue and is spared some criteria, including the capital and business-activity limits. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, fns 1, 8]
- **To Risk:** A licensee must redeem at par, generally within one business day, and hold reserves on trust with a qualified custodian. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.5.1-2.5.4, 3.3.3]

1. Explanatory Note on Licensing of Stablecoin Issuers — HKMA — Jul 2025 — read Chapters 2 and 3 for scope, offerors and AI carve-outs — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Explanatory_Notes_on_Licensing_of_Stablecoin_Issuers_eng.pdf

title: Supervisory Incubator for DLT
md:
An HKMA channel where a bank can test a distributed ledger technology (DLT) product with a dedicated supervisory team before full launch.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot (open to Authorized Institutions) [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] |
| Started | 8 Jan 2025 [S:fae36c380174, p.1, footnote 1] |
| Next official date | None stated |
| Covered in | B2, B3, C5, E2, E3 |

## What it is

The Incubator is a supervisory arrangement to help banks manage the risks of adopting DLT. It pays particular attention to services that span DLT and legacy systems. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2] Tokenised deposits were a core focus from the start. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2] For a single bank, it offers one contact point to confirm that risk controls are adequate before launch, with a dedicated HKMA team and optional live trials. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] Trials are run in a hands-on, step-by-step way. [S:fae36c380174, p.1] At industry level, it shares good practice through guidance, sharing sessions and research. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 4] In October 2025 the HKMA Chief Executive wrote that six banks had launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Apr 2024 | HKMA issues DLT risk-management considerations | In force | [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1] |
| 8 Jan 2025 | Incubator launched at FiNETech4; circular to banks | Pilot | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2, 5]; [S:fae36c380174, p.1, footnote 1] |
| 24 Oct 2025 | HKMA reports six banks' tokenised deposit services launched via the Incubator | Pilot | [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section] |
| 9 Mar 2026 | Business-model circular suggests small real-world trials through the Incubator | In force | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] |
| Mar 2026 | HKMA event on Ensemble and the Incubator for about 60 banks | Pilot | [S:38e1f67c38df, paras 3, 6-7] |

## What it means for your bank

- Use is optional. It is a way to confirm DLT risk management before full launch, not a licence. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]
- A bank in the Incubator may get some supervisory flexibility, decided case by case, on factors like those used in the Fintech Supervisory Sandbox. [S:fae36c380174, p.1, footnote 2]
- That flexibility assumes the bank manages trial risks in line with the trial's scale and nature. [S:fae36c380174, p.1]
- Where a legal or regulatory construct is inadvertently incompatible with DLT, the HKMA says it will consider adapting its approach. [S:fae36c380174, p.2]
- The HKMA's DLT risk-management expectations still apply: board responsibility, network choice, smart contracts, settlement finality and key security. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 1-8]
- New digital-asset activity still needs prior discussion with the HKMA. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Incubator entry is not approval; any flexibility is case by case and tied to trial controls. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and footnote 2]
- **To business heads:** Six banks have launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator, according to the HKMA. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA's business-model circular invites banks to use the Incubator for small real-world trials of new models. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- **To Risk:** The HKMA holds the board and senior management fully responsible for DLT adoption and its risks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]

## Key documents

1. Supervisory Incubator for Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) — HKMA circular — 8 Jan 2025 — read both pages, including footnote 2 — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250120-1-EN/20250120-1-EN.pdf
2. HKMA launches Supervisory Incubator to foster responsible adoption of DLT — HKMA — 8 Jan 2025 — read paras 2-4 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/01/20250108-3/

title: Tokenised Bond Expert Group and the DLT fixed-income law review
md:
An HKMA industry panel on tokenised bonds, working alongside a joint FSTB–HKMA review of whether Hong Kong law fits bonds held on a distributed ledger (DLT).

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for the Expert Group (TBEG); Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and HKMA for the review [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 1]; [S:279f10054c6e, opening paragraph] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Exploratory (TBEG); review phase 1 conclusions published 29 Jun 2026 [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-3]; [S:279f10054c6e, opening paragraph] |
| Started | Review first announced in the 2025-26 Budget; TBEG convened 5 Jun 2026 [S:279f10054c6e, closing paragraph]; [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 1] |
| Next official date | Phase 2 legal review in H2 2026 (stated target) [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase' section]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |
| Covered in | C5, A3, E1, E3 |

## What it is

Policy Statement 2.0 said the FSTB and HKMA would review the legal and regulatory position on tokenisation, starting with bonds. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 9] The 2026-27 Budget said the Government would issue guidance confirming that debenture-holder registers may be kept on a DLT. It also said it would explore e-signatures and digitised bearer bonds. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107] The HKMA convened the TBEG in June 2026. Its members come from industry bodies, financial institutions, law firms and infrastructure and technology providers. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2] The group's May 2026 discussions fed into the joint review. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 3] Phase 1 concluded that current law is already flexible enough for tokenised bond issues. [S:279f10054c6e, opening paragraph] On the same day, the Companies Registry published FAQs. They confirm that a DLT-based register of debenture holders can meet Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) record-keeping rules. [S:279f10054c6e, 'Issuing clarifications on DLT record keeping' section]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26 Jun 2025 | Policy Statement 2.0 commits to a tokenisation law review, starting with bonds | Stated target | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 9] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget sets review directions: DLT registers, e-signatures, bearer bonds | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107] |
| May 2026 | First TBEG discussion sessions | Exploratory | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 3] |
| 5 Jun 2026 | HKMA announces the TBEG | Exploratory | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 1] |
| 29 Jun 2026 | Phase 1 findings and Companies Registry FAQs | Conclusions published | [S:279f10054c6e, opening paragraph and 'Issuing clarifications on DLT record keeping' section] |
| H2 2026 | Phase 2 legislative review (e-execution; possession and transfer of tokens) | Stated target | [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase' section] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: TBEG to launch the phase 2 review with the FSTB | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- No new obligation arises. Phase 1 found the existing framework adequate, so current securities and company rules keep applying to tokenised bonds. [S:279f10054c6e, opening paragraph]
- If the bank keeps or relies on a DLT debenture register for a Hong Kong issuer, the Companies Registry FAQs are the reference point. [S:279f10054c6e, 'Issuing clarifications on DLT record keeping' section]
- Phase 2 will look at electronic signatures for trusts linked to tokenised bonds and funds. It will also look at how possession and transfer work for tokenised fixed-income instruments. Trustee and custody teams should track it. [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase' section]
- The HKMA says it will review and update the group's membership when needed. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 4]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Phase 1 changed no law; it confirmed flexibility and added Companies Registry FAQs on DLT registers. [S:279f10054c6e, opening paragraph and 'Issuing clarifications on DLT record keeping' section]
- **To business heads:** Phase 2 targets e-execution of issue documents, which could speed tokenised bond launches. [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase' section]
- **To the CEO:** The TBEG is the HKMA's industry channel on tokenised bond policy and practice. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2]
- **To Risk:** Possession and transfer of tokenised instruments remain under legal review; findings are not yet published. [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase' section]

title: New VA licensing regimes: dealing, custody, advisory and management
md:
Four planned statutory licensing regimes for virtual-asset (VA) intermediaries, to be brought in by one bill under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO, Cap. 615).

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and Securities and Futures Commission (SFC); HKMA as frontline regulator for banks [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Conclusions published (all four regimes) [S:ff3df4326e0f, para 2]; [S:4a0342268bf2, paras 2-3] |
| Started | VA OTC proposal, 8 Feb 2024; widened in the 27 Jun 2025 consultations [S:efcdb0ae3849, para 2.6]; [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1] |
| Next official date | Single bill to LegCo later in 2026 (stated target); commencement not set [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 32] |
| Covered in | E1, C1, C3, A3, B2 |

## What it is

The regimes will replace today's approach of attaching VA terms and conditions to SFC licences and registrations under the joint circular. The joint circular's current requirements become the baseline. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] VA dealing will align with Type 1 (dealing in securities). Dealers must keep client VAs with SFC-regulated VA custodians. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 3-5, 26] A custodian licence attaches to whoever safekeeps private keys and can move client VAs. Custody of tokenised securities falls outside it. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6-8, 12] VA advisory will mirror Type 4 and VA management Type 9. Banks may register for these rather than be licensed. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10] An earlier plan for a Customs-run licence for VA-for-cash trading was folded into the SFC dealing regime. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.9-1.10]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 Feb 2024 | VA OTC licensing consultation (Customs-run; banks exempt) | Superseded | [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23] |
| 19 Feb 2025 | SFC ASPIRe roadmap lists OTC and custody licensing | Exploratory | [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1] |
| 27 Jun 2025 | Dealing and custodian consultations (to 29 Aug 2025) | Superseded | [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1] |
| 24 Dec 2025 | Dealing and custodian conclusions; advisory and management consultation | Conclusions published | [S:ff3df4326e0f, paras 2, 5] |
| 23 Jan 2026 | Advisory and management consultation closes | Superseded | [S:6186c01c6649, para 72] |
| 26 May 2026 | Advisory and management conclusions | Conclusions published | [S:4a0342268bf2, paras 2-3] |
| 24 Jun 2026 | Government: one bill for all four regimes later in 2026 | Stated target | [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: SFC to enhance VA licensing regimes | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(i)] |

## What it means for your bank

- A bank will register with the SFC for these activities; the HKMA stays its frontline regulator. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]
- No deeming or grandfathering is planned. Firms already vetted by the SFC or HKMA get an expedited track. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]
- A bank VA custodian would use existing HKMA capital rules, not the custodian capital baseline. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42]
- VA management has no de minimis threshold. Any discretionary VA exposure needs a licence or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 32]
- Advice on a mixed VA and securities portfolio still needs the VA advisory permission for the VA part. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 21]
- Once the regimes apply, no one may actively market these services to the Hong Kong public without SFC licensing or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 70]
- Early pre-application talks with the SFC, or the HKMA as applicable, are encouraged. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]; [S:4a0342268bf2, para 6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** All four regimes have conclusions; one bill is targeted for 2026 and no grandfathering is planned. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]
- **To business heads:** Inventory every VA dealing, custody, advisory and management line now; even small discretionary VA exposure will need registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 32]
- **To the CEO:** Commencement dates are not set; the Government and SFC will weigh how long the market needs to adjust. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- **To Risk:** Under the dealing regime, client VAs must sit with SFC-regulated custodians only. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]
